sources.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
sources.source_type: IETF Standards Track RFC; primary protocol specification
sources.locator: §8.8.1–8.8.3 (validators, Last-Modified, ETag); §13.1.2–13.1.3 (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since); §15.4.5 (304); §12.5.5 Vary; §15.4.5 304 Not Modified
sources.observed_operation: web__run search/open/find on the official RFC HTML; no request was sent to a case URL.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Last-Modified reports the origin server's believed modification time of the selected representation; the determination is implementation-specific.
Last-Modified is implicitly weak unless RFC clock/resolution conditions permit it to be treated as strong.
ETag is an opaque validator for selected representations, not necessarily a cryptographic digest.
If-None-Match uses weak comparison for GET cache validation, so matching may validate even if representation data changed.
If-Modified-Since is ignored when If-None-Match is present; dates are fallback validators, not proof of byte identity.

Vary identifies request fields that may have selected the response representation; it expands the matching key, and Vary:* means the variant may depend on other factors the client cannot fully reproduce.
A 304 response has no content body and returns only specified metadata for cache updates; it is not the new representation body and cannot itself re-resolve passage anchors.
sources.applicability: Defines online-check claims; keep validator outcome separate from local byte hash, source version and claim applicability. Record the selected representation's media type/language, Vary fields and safe variant inputs; treat Vary:* or non-reproducible selection as variant-unknown.

additional_access_events.observed_operation: web__run opened RFC 9110 §12.5.5 and §15.4.5 and found Vary/304 passages.
Independent critic web__run open/find on RFC Editor HTML §§8.8.1–8.8.3, 12.5.5, 13.1.2, 15.4.2–15.4.9: validators, Vary, 304, and redirect status meanings.

sources.title: RFC 9111 — HTTP Caching
sources.source_type: IETF Standards Track RFC; primary caching specification
sources.observed_operation: web__run search/open/find on official RFC HTML sections on heuristic freshness and validation.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A cache may calculate heuristic freshness only when explicit freshness is absent and the response is eligible; Last-Modified can inform an estimate.
Freshness is cache-reuse policy, and successful validation can update cache metadata; neither determines whether a technical claim applies to a release.
Conditional validators support cache revalidation; handbook evidence semantics are a separate layer.
sources.applicability: Avoid presenting cache-fresh/cache-stale policy as a conclusion about note validity.

sources.title: RFC 6920 — Naming Things with Hashes
sources.source_type: IETF Standards Track RFC; primary hash-name specification
sources.locator: §2 Hashes Are What Count; §3 Named Information URI; §10 Security Considerations
sources.observed_operation: web__run opened the official RFC HTML and read hash-based naming, SHA-256 support and security context.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A full digest and algorithm can identify digital-object bytes and bind retrieved bytes to a name if integrity is checked.
RFC 6920 leaves hash input to the application/protocol; specify whether the digest is over raw bytes or normalized text.
A hash alone does not prove publisher identity, semantic version or applicability; a hash does not protect confidentiality.
sources.applicability: Supports raw-byte and extracted-text digests, with separate publisher/version metadata; do not send note-derived digests upstream.

sources.title: RFC 7089 — HTTP Memento
sources.source_type: IETF Informational RFC; primary description of Memento
sources.locator: §2.1.1 Accept-Datetime/Memento-Datetime; §3.1 Datetime Negotiation; §4.5.6 Sticky Memento-Datetime/original link
sources.observed_operation: web__run search/open/find on RFC Editor HTML, including datetime negotiation and byte-equivalence caveat.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: A TimeGate chooses a best-fit Memento at its discretion; returned date may differ significantly from requested date.
A Memento response carries Memento-Datetime and a link to the original; conforming Memento servers keep these identifiers sticky.
A replay may not be byte-for-byte equal to the original because of format migrations, URI rewriting or archive banners.
sources.applicability: Optional recovery trail for moved pages; retrieved archive capture is another edition and should be hashed locally.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.locator: §4.2.4 Text Quote Selector; §4.2.5 Text Position Selector; §4.3 States; §4.3.1 Time State; §4.3.2 Request Header State
sources.observed_operation: web__run opened the dated Recommendation and selector anchors; find located selector definitions and brittleness note.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: TextQuoteSelector stores normalized exact text and may store prefix/suffix context.
TextPositionSelector uses normalized Unicode code-point offsets, zero-based with end exclusive.
Position selectors are brittle under edits; the Recommendation recommends an additional State to identify the correct representation.
A State describes how to retrieve the intended representation; Time State can identify a historical representation and Request Header State describes headers for the intended variant.
A response representation may also depend on non-header context such as client IP; recording headers may not be sufficient to recreate it.
sources.applicability: Use quote/context plus edition identity and structural locator; position is only a hint within the pinned edition. Keep copied note excerpts local. Store only safe representation-selection metadata needed for public sources; never persist/replay credentials or unrelated private headers.

additional_access_events.observed_operation: web__run opened the dated Recommendation's Time State and Request Header State anchors.
Independent critic web__run open/find on the dated W3C Recommendation: Text Quote/Position Selectors and §4.3 States, including representation state and position-selector brittleness.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.observed_operation: web__run opened the dated W3C Recommendation and located derivation/revision entries.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: PROV distinguishes entities and derivation/revision relations and provides specific relations for applicable cases.
Using the vocabulary does not require deploying RDF/OWL; edges still need evidence and assertion context.
sources.applicability: Represent explicit edition lineage and note-to-evidence provenance without claiming semantic interchangeability.

sources.title: Git data model documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: No numbered edition or immutable commit is identified on the accessed page; living documentation accessed 2026-10-12
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Git commits/files are objects with IDs derived from object type and contents; objects do not change after creation and their contents can be recovered while retained.
References/tags name objects; preserve repository identity and full resolved object ID rather than relying only on a human-readable name.
sources.applicability: For Git-hosted docs, retain repository URI, release/tag label, resolved full commit/object ID and path. Other media need other edition identity.

sources.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension documentation
sources.source_type: Official SQLite primary documentation; living page
sources.released_version_or_commit: Living docs; FTS5 is included in the amalgamation since SQLite 3.9.0 (2015-10-14); source-tree builds require enablement and build defaults differ.
sources.locator: §2.1 build/enablement; §4.4.3 External Content Tables; §4.4.4 External Content Table Pitfalls; §6.3 Rebuild; §6.4 Integrity Check
sources.observed_operation: web__run opened official FTS5 documentation and located external-content behavior, trigger example, rebuild and integrity-check.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: External-content FTS5 reads row values from a separate content table; the application is responsible for consistency.
Triggers only track later mutations; an initial build/rebuild is required for rows that predate triggers.
Rebuild can repopulate from current content; integrity-check can compare the external content when configured as documented.
FTS5 availability depends on the linked SQLite build; verify the actual runtime.
sources.applicability: Candidate for local search over edition text; result rows must map to immutable edition IDs. Performance is unmeasured.

sources.title: SQLite bug forum: FTS5 external-content index and nested AFTER UPDATE triggers
sources.source_type: Public SQLite Fossil bug-forum report and maintainer discussion; report record, not specification
sources.released_version_or_commit: Thread opened 2026-08-04; report says reproduced on 3.45.1, 3.45.3 and 3.53.2; maintainer response 2026-08-05; no fix commit identified in this thread.
sources.observed_operation: web__run opened the official SQLite forum thread and read report, reporter correction, and maintainer response.
governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The first reproduction omitted an insert-sync trigger and was challenged; the reporter corrected it and posted a refined case.
Maintainer confirmed an illustrative nested-trigger ordering issue and said FTS5 advice does not work in that combination; suggested FTS trigger creation last may work in practice.
This does not establish that all external-content FTS uses fail. No local reproduction or fix was performed here.
sources.applicability: Risk for mutable external-content rows plus nested AFTER UPDATE triggers. Prefer append-only edition text; if mutable integration remains, test exact packaged build and inspect later release history.
